description.narrative: The Risk-Informed Development for Resilience (RID4R) project, implemented by DoDMA with support from UNDP, aims to strengthen Malawi’s resilience to climate-related and other hazards through risk-informed development planning and systems enhancement. The project is aligned with the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction, the Malawi 2063 vision, the National Resilience Strategy (NRS), and the 2023 Disaster Risk Management Act.RID4R adopts a systems approach to resilience by enhancing anticipatory, absorptive, adaptive, and transformative capacities at national, district, and community levels. Specifically, the project seeks to:Strengthen disaster response and preparedness systems for multi-hazard scenarios, building anticipatory capacities.Promote risk-informed planning, financing, and accountability frameworks that address the underlying drivers of vulnerability.The project targets vulnerable communities within five local authorities—Nkhotakota, Salima, Dedza, Zomba City, and Mzuzu City—which have experienced significant impacts from disasters, including Cyclone Freddy in 2023 and El Niño-induced dry spells in 2024. These districts have recorded substantial losses in productive sectors, public infrastructure, and basic services. For instance, Cyclone Freddy caused widespread destruction of homes, schools, health facilities, and roads, while Lake Malawi backflows in Salima and Nkhotakota disrupted livelihoods and access to critical services.Drawing on lessons from the previous DRM4R initiative, RID4R emphasizes inclusive implementation, community engagement, institutional capacity strengthening, and the creation of knowledge systems for informed decision-making. Activities are underpinned by extensive stakeholder consultations and technical inputs coordinated through a reference group led by DoDMA and UNDP.RID4R contributes to the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) Outcome 4 and UNDP Country Programme Document (CPD

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

The Implementing Partner shall ensure that all of its obligations set forth under the section entitled “Legal Context and/or Risk Management Standard Clauses” are passed on to each responsible party, subcontractor and sub-recipient and that all the clauses under this section entitled “Risk Management” are included, mutatis mutandis, in all sub-contracts or sub-agreements entered into further to the Project Document
